title: Twilight release playtest journal
content:
Purpose: quick diary for late-shift canary playtests — small, quiet traffic windows; focus on safety, repeatability, and fast rollback. This is a personal scratchpad (not official runbook).

TL;DR plan (two-hour window):
- 00:00-00:10: pre-warm cohort, send traffic to warmup clients (cohort A, 0.5% of traffic).
- 00:10-00:30: steady-state observe; turn on slow-metrics (latency p95/p99, err rate by tenant, cost per token)
- 00:30-01:00: increment to 2% (cohort B), enable QA probes + semantic quality checks (prompt set x3).
- 01:00-01:40: if stable, 5% for selective clients + run end-to-end trace samples.
- 01:40-02:00: roll back to baseline or continue to warm-up for next day.

Checklist (my copy):
- [ ] Confirm model pin mapping in config-store: model: v2.3.1 -> variant: quant-8-fp16.
- [ ] Ensure canary flag key: rollout/twilight/2026-03-11 exists and points to cohort buckets.
- [ ] Pre-deploy smoke: run local generate with seq_len=1024 on dedicated staging to verify KV cache correctness.
- [ ] Notify SRE on-call and leave channel open; paste run commands and TTL.
- [ ] Prepare rollback tag and pre-approved hotfix branch (pr #987).

Quick commands (for me):
- Toggle canary via API: curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/flags/rollout/twilight/2026-03-11 --data '{"state":"on","buckets":[{"cohort":"A","pct":0.5}]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Query latency: grafana/api/metrics?query=avg_over_time(request_duration_ms_p99[5m])&cohort=twilight
- Fetch recent traces: curl https://traces.internal/api/query?tag=rollout:twilight&limit=50

Safety thresholds (my heuristics):
- Immediate abort: err rate > 0.3% absolute increase over baseline or 10x jump in 5m error spikes.
- Soft pause: p99 latency + 150ms over baseline sustained for 20m.
- Quality guardrails: semantic drift score (prompt-set A) drops by >1.5 pts.
- Cost spike: per-token cost increase > 25% for canary traffic compared to baseline -> escalate to optimizer.

Observability notes (what I watch):
- p50/p95/p99 latency by route and model variant
- Error spikes with early signs (timeout, OOM, fallback triggers)
- Token rate and average tokens per request (warmup impact)
- Top slow clients (by 95th latency) — sudden changes often signal client-side input diff
- Semantic quality: run 3 gold-prompts through the canary and score against baseline using micro-eval harness (local).

Warmup strategy rationale:
- Prefix caching dependency: heavy-tail clients benefit from pre-warmed KV caches. If we send a small fraction of consistent traffic first, we reduce initial OOMs and p99 spikes once ramped.
- Use same client signatures where possible (repeat prompts) for first 10m to prime caches.

Pinning details to record:
- Service config: inference.model_pin = "gptx-v2.3.1-quant8"
- SDK flag: client.override_model = false (ensure no client-side pin).
- Rollback tag: repo@release/twilight-2026-03-11. If rollback required, deploy repo@release/twilight-rollback-2026-03-11 (hotfix branch).

Post-playtest snippets (expected to fill during run):
- 00:18 - small p99 blip on route /chat/send, traced to a heavy prompt (id 0x33f). Note: follow up with client to check prompt length distribution.
- 00:46 - semantic score down 0.6 on prompt-set A; still within tolerance but watch trend.
- 01:12 - two OOM fallbacks in worker-pool-12 (AZ-us-west2-b); pinned quant kernels might need kernel-tuning.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- How aggressive should the warmup repetition be for multi-tenant clients? (1x repeat vs 3x)
- If semantic drift shows slow degradation, what's the automatic rollback cadence? do we abort immediately or step down fractionally?
- Confirm whether the optimizer can auto-switch to a cheaper variant on cost spike without impacting quality (need product decision).

Notes-to-self re: client comms:
- Keep customer-facing note short: "We ran a low-traffic test of new model tuning tonight; no customer impact observed. We'll update if we proceed further."
- If rollback: standard message template + note about timeline and what to expect in next window.

Postmortem checklist (if anything goes wrong):
- Dump traces and attach to JIRA-4521
- Capture model pin state and exact commit hash
- Snapshot config-store rollout key and any toggles used
- Collect 30m of pre/post metrics and compare with baseline
- Tag related PRs and assign to on-call and model-owner for next action

Quick heuristics (mnemonic): SLOW-HEAT
- S: Start tiny (0.5%)
- L: Look at latency, logs, and LRU cache metrics
- O: Observe semantic quality quickly (gold prompts)
- W: Warm prefixes, repeat a few times
- H: Have rollback branch ready
- E: Escalate quickly if thresholds hit
- A: Annotate events in the runbook
- T: Tidy up artifacts and close the canary flag after finishing

Endnotes: this is my relaxed template for small evening windows. Copy it into official runbook once we validate it over 3 consecutive safe runs. Keep it terse so it's usable at 2am.

-- Alex
